label: late original-phase input (t>=5) after r/3/l/o/x/f seen
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t >= 5) & seen([tok("r"), tok("3"), tok("l"), tok("o"), tok("x"), tok("f")])
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase, never at t<3, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase. Rate rises with position (orig_idx 6-7 ~42% active, t=5-7 hold ~85% of mass) and near the end of the input (to_go 0-2), so longer sequences (L=8-9) carry most mass. Within late positions it is content-gated by an accumulated prefix: much more likely once tokens like r, 3, l (strongest), o, x, f have appeared earlier (prev2_tok r/3/l lift ~2.5x); top activations are 2-4 steps after an r or 3. Activations usually come in consecutive runs that ramp up and decay. Slightly higher on first occurrences of the input token. The simple position predicate (phase 0, t>=5) gets recall 0.88 but precision 0.34; adding the seen-token condition raises F1 only to ~0.56, so the content dependence looks like a graded, distributed accumulation that a token-set predicate cannot capture fully.
